     NOTATION.md has no symbol for it. Opened as ISSUES.md item 9. -->

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What it does.** Nudges the first interior cell row above the physical lower $x_1$ boundary toward a target
temperature, velocity, or composition with a time scale $\tau$.
**Switch.** `relax-bot-temp: {tau, btemp, at-face}` (`btemp` required, `at-face` default `false`);
`relax-bot-velo: {tau, bvx, bvy, bvz}` (targets default 0); `relax-bot-comp: {tau, species, xfrac}`
($\sum$`xfrac` $\le1$). $\tau>0$ [s] for all three. Each off unless its key is present.
**Order.** Explicit relaxation, first order in time per stage; the at-face target is exact for a linear $T$.
**Defining equation.** @eq-ch09-relax-temp, @eq-ch09-relax-velo and @eq-ch09-relax-comp.
:::

The three modules stand in for a surface layer that the grid does not resolve. Each acts only in the bottom row of
interior cells and only on the block that owns the physical lower $x_1$ boundary. `relax-bot-temp` adds heat at
constant volume to bring the temperature toward `btemp`; with `at-face: true` it relaxes the temperature
extrapolated to the lower face instead of the cell value, because a prescribed surface temperature is a value at
the face. `relax-bot-velo` adds a momentum drag toward the target velocity, lowered to covariant components on the
cubed sphere. `relax-bot-comp` exchanges mass between dry air and the named species at fixed density and
temperature, with the internal-energy change computed by kintera.

None of the three changes the total energy for the momentum part: `relax-bot-velo` leaves $E$ untouched, so the
kinetic energy it removes becomes internal energy, as for the sponges (@sec-ch09-sponge).

*Aliases.* chengcli/snapy#219 introduced `at-face` with the uniform-grid weights $1.5$/$-0.5$ and the gain
$1/1.5$; #279 generalised them to the coordinate spacing.

### Derivation

#### Temperature

Let cell $0$ be the bottom interior cell and cell $1$ the one above it, with centroids $x_{1,0}$, $x_{1,1}$ and the
lower face at $x_{1,-1/2}$. The cell form adds, in one stage,

$$
\Delta E_0 = \frac{\Delta t}{\tau}\,\rho_0c_{v,0}\,(T_{\mathrm b} - T^{\mathrm{tgt}}),
$$ {#eq-ch09-relax-temp}

with $T_{\mathrm b}$ = `btemp` and $T^{\mathrm{tgt}}=T_0$ ([`relax_bot_temp.cpp:80-104`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/relax_bot_temp.cpp#L80-L104)). With `at-face` the
target is the linear extrapolation of the two cell values to the face,

$$
\begin{aligned}
T^{\mathrm{tgt}} &= (1+\alpha_{\mathrm f})\,T_0 - \alpha_{\mathrm f}\,T_1, \\
\alpha_{\mathrm f} &= \frac{x_{1,0} - x_{1,-1/2}}{x_{1,1} - x_{1,0}},
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch09-relax-face}

and the increment is multiplied by the gain $1/(1+\alpha_{\mathrm f})$, `gain`
([`relax_bot_temp.cpp:82-103`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/relax_bot_temp.cpp#L82-L103)).
The target is exact for a linear $T$ on any spacing [check `src/snapy_report/ch09/relax_check.py`, output
`relax_check.out`, `[C1]`]; on uniform cells $\alpha_{\mathrm f}=\tfrac12$, the target is $1.5T_0-0.5T_1$ and the
gain $\tfrac23$ (`[C2]`). The gain follows from the chain rule: only cell $0$ is heated, and
$\partial T^{\mathrm{tgt}}/\partial T_0 = 1+\alpha_{\mathrm f}$, so heating cell $0$ at $(T_{\mathrm b}-T^{\mathrm{tgt}})/ [\tau(1+\alpha_{\mathrm f})]$ moves the face value at exactly $(T_{\mathrm b}-T^{\mathrm{tgt}})/\tau$ (`[C3]`).

#### Velocity

With $\mathbf v_{\mathrm b}$ = (`bvx`, `bvy`, `bvz`) the target for the contravariant components
$(v^1, v^2, v^3)$ of the bottom cell,

$$
\Delta m_{a} = \frac{\Delta t}{\tau}\,\rho_0\,g_{ab}\,(v_{\mathrm b}^{b} - v_0^{b}),
$$ {#eq-ch09-relax-velo}

where $g_{ab}$ lowers the index; it is the identity on orthogonal grids and on the cubed sphere has
$g_{23}=\cos\theta_{jk}$; the force is lowered with `coord_vec_lower_` ([`relax_bot_velo.cpp:65-75`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/relax_bot_velo.cpp#L65-L75)),
whose kernel is `coord_vec_lower_impl` ([`coord_utils_impl.h:19-24`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/coord_utils_impl.h#L19-L24)). The argument for lowering is the one of @sec-ch09-sponge: the stored
momenta are covariant, and an unlowered force rotates the wind instead of braking it.

#### Composition

Let $y_n$ be the mass fractions of the species $n=1..N_y$ in the bottom cell, $\rho$ the total density, and $y^{\mathrm{tgt}}_n$
the mass fractions of the target state: the current mole fractions with the named species set to `xfrac` and dry
air taking the rest, converted back to mass fractions. One stage adds

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Delta\rho_{\mathrm d} &= -\frac{\Delta t}{\tau}\,\rho\sum_n(y^{\mathrm{tgt}}_n - y_n), \\
\Delta(\rho y_n) &= \frac{\Delta t}{\tau}\,\rho\,(y^{\mathrm{tgt}}_n - y_n), \\
\Delta E &= \frac{\Delta t}{\tau}\,\big[U(\rho y^{\mathrm{tgt}}, T) - U(\rho y, T)\big],
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch09-relax-comp}

as `delta` ([`relax_bot_comp.cpp:95-117`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/relax_bot_comp.cpp#L95-L117)). The total density is unchanged (`[C4]`) and the momentum is untouched.
$U(\cdot, T)$ is kintera's volumetric internal energy at the cell temperature, `VT->U`
([`kintera thermo_y.cpp:240-245`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77/src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp#L240-L245)), with the partial densities from `DY->V`
([`kintera thermo_y.cpp:212-226`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77/src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp#L212-L226)) and the mole/mass conversions `Y->X` ([`kintera thermo_y.cpp:196-211`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77/src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp#L196-L211))
and `X->Y` ([`kintera thermo_x.cpp:140-150`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77/src/thermo/thermo_x.cpp#L140-L150)). So the swap is isothermal provided kintera's $U$ is the same
function as snapy's equation of state uses; the test below checks that for the ideal-moist fixture.

*Exact and truncated.* All three are explicit relaxations: for $\Delta t\ll\tau$ the bottom row approaches its target
as $e^{-t/\tau}$ to first order in $\Delta t/\tau$; with $\Delta t=\tau$ the composition reaches its target in one
step, which the test uses.

### Numerical method

@fig-ch09-relax-face shows the at-face target.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch09-relax-face
#| fig-cap: "The at-face target of relax-bot-temp on uniform cells ($\\alpha_{\\mathrm f}=\\tfrac12$). Sky-blue circles: the temperatures $T_0$ and $T_1$ in $\\mathrm K$ of the bottom cell and the one above it; bluish-green dashed line and diamond: their linear extrapolation $T^{\\mathrm{tgt}}=1.5\\,T_0-0.5\\,T_1$ to the lower face (thick black line), the value that is relaxed toward $T_{\\mathrm b}$ = btemp (dotted blue line)."
#| fig-alt: "Two cells above a wall, two temperature points, a dashed line through them extended to the wall ending in a diamond, and a horizontal dotted target line above."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch09.fig_relax_face import make_fig
make_fig()
```

The modules read the bottom row of interior cells and, for `at-face`, the row above it; they read no ghost. `at-face`
needs two interior cells in the row selection, which `PartOptions::depth` caps at $n_g$, so it requires
$n_g\ge2$ ([`relax_bot_temp.cpp:86-92`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/relax_bot_temp.cpp#L86-L92)). They run in every stage, explicit, in the forcing loop
(@sec-ch09-framework).

: Code map of the bottom relaxations. {#tbl-ch09-relax-code}

1. Each `from_yaml` checks keys and values: $\tau>0$; `btemp` present and positive; `at-face` a literal
   `true`/`false`; `species` and `xfrac` of equal length, no duplicates, each `xfrac` in $[0,1]$, sum $\le1$
   (`RelaxBotTempOptionsImpl::from_yaml`, [`relax_bot_temp.cpp:15-45`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/relax_bot_temp.cpp#L15-L45);
   `RelaxBotVeloOptionsImpl::from_yaml`, [`relax_bot_velo.cpp:17-34`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/relax_bot_velo.cpp#L17-L34);
   `RelaxBotCompOptionsImpl::from_yaml`, [`relax_bot_comp.cpp:20-52`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/relax_bot_comp.cpp#L20-L52)).
2. `RelaxBotCompImpl::reset` builds its own kintera `ThermoY` and `ThermoX`, and refuses an unknown species or the
   dry species ([`relax_bot_comp.cpp:61-80`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/relax_bot_comp.cpp#L61-L80)).
3. Each `forward` returns at once unless the lower $x_1$ face is physical, then adds its increment to the bottom row
   ([`relax_bot_temp.cpp:58-106`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/relax_bot_temp.cpp#L58-L106), [`relax_bot_velo.cpp:47-77`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/relax_bot_velo.cpp#L47-L77),
   [`relax_bot_comp.cpp:82-119`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/relax_bot_comp.cpp#L82-L119)).

### Limits

1. **`at-face` cost stability** on the one initial condition tried (chengcli/snapy#219 Limits); it is off by
   default. Not re-measured.
2. **kintera's $U$ against snapy's.** `relax_bottom_composition_preserves_state` shows the swap is isothermal for
   the ideal-moist fixture `test_diffusion_moist.yaml` (constant heat capacities). For the moist-mixture equation of
   state, or species with temperature-dependent heat capacities, it is not tested.
3. **`btemp` default.** The options struct defaults `btemp` to 300 K ([`forcing.hpp:450-451`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/forcing/forcing.hpp#L450-L451)), but YAML
   requires it; a Python user who builds the options directly gets 300 K silently.
4. **Velocity target naming.** `bvx`, `bvy`, `bvz` are the targets of $v^1$, $v^2$, $v^3$; with $x_1$ vertical,
   `bvx` is the vertical target, not an $x$ component.
5. **Energy of the velocity drag.** $E$ is untouched, so the removed kinetic energy heats the bottom row; intended
   for a drag, but not stated in the code.
6. **Solids.** The modules read the solid placeholder state if a solid cell sits in the bottom row
   (`sources/canoe__diffusion_ghost_TECH_REPORT.md` §7). Not tested.
